coverage.definition_review: Every definition, alias, category, example and source field was read semantically. External retrieval targeted nuanced, product, changing and corrected claims; this is not 166 independently sourced mini-literature-reviews.

findings.original: The column or group of columns chosen to uniquely identify each row in a table. A primary key cannot contain a null value.
findings.correction: The column or columns chosen to uniquely identify each row. SQL requires primary keys to be non-null, but implementations have exceptions, notably some SQLite table definitions.
findings.reason: The original universal SQL implementation claim fails for ordinary SQLite rowid tables.

findings.original: Time to live. In a cache it usually means how long an entry is valid. In an IP packet it limits how many routing hops the packet can survive.
findings.correction: Time to live. In a cache it usually limits how long an entry is valid. IPv4 TTL is reduced at each router, limiting forwarding hops; IPv6 calls its corresponding field Hop Limit.
findings.reason: Distinguish IPv4 TTL and IPv6 Hop Limit without implying all IP packets carry a field named TTL.

findings.original: Marking or removing a cached value because it is no longer valid. This prevents readers from continuing to use an outdated copy.
findings.correction: Marking or removing a cached value because it is no longer valid. Preventing stale reads also requires handling concurrent reads, refills and propagation delays.
findings.reason: Invalidation alone does not prevent a concurrent stale refill or an already-started read.

findings.original: Many requests miss the same cached value at once and all try to rebuild it, overloading the underlying service.
findings.correction: Many requests miss the same cached value at once and try to rebuild it, potentially overloading the underlying service.
findings.reason: Stampedes create overload risk, not inevitable overload at every request rate.

findings.original: A consensus algorithm that uses a leader, replicated logs and elections to keep a cluster’s state in agreement.
findings.correction: A consensus algorithm that uses leader elections and replicated logs to agree on committed commands. Followers can lag while preserving the protocol’s safety guarantees.
findings.reason: Consensus safety does not imply every replica always has an identical current state.

findings.original: A way for a slower consumer to signal that producers should slow down, preventing unbounded queues and resource use.
findings.correction: A way for a slower consumer to signal that producers should slow down. When respected throughout the pipeline, it helps limit queue growth and resource use.
findings.reason: Signalling alone cannot bound a pipeline whose upstream ignores the signal or buffers without bounds.

findings.original: Unsynchronised concurrent access to the same memory location where at least one access is a write. Its consequences depend on the language’s memory model.
findings.correction: Conflicting memory accesses without the ordering required by a language’s memory model. In C++, at least one must be non-atomic; accesses using only atomics are not automatically data races.
findings.reason: Relaxed atomic writes are unsynchronised but excluded from the C++ data-race definition; lifetime conflicts also need not be ordinary writes.

findings.original: Tracking how many references point to an object and reclaiming it when that count reaches zero. Cycles need additional handling.
findings.correction: Tracking strong references to an object so that reaching zero can trigger reclamation. Weak references do not keep it alive, and reference cycles need additional handling.
findings.reason: Clarify strong references and avoid promising immediate reclamation across all implementations.

findings.original: The order in which the bytes of a multibyte value are stored. Little-endian stores the least significant byte first; big-endian stores the most significant first.
findings.correction: The byte order of a multibyte value. In memory, little-endian places the least significant byte at the lowest address; big-endian places the most significant byte there.
findings.reason: First is ambiguous between memory addresses, display order and transmission order.

findings.original: Saving a function’s result for particular inputs so repeated calls can reuse it.
findings.correction: Saving a function’s result for particular inputs so repeated calls can reuse it. Reuse is valid only while the result and any relevant external state remain applicable.
findings.reason: Cached results from time, randomness or changing external state need invalidation or a different cache key.

findings.original: Learning patterns or structure from data without a target answer supplied for every example.
findings.correction: Learning patterns or structure from data without supplied target labels guiding the learning objective, for example by clustering similar examples.
findings.reason: Original without a target for every example also describes semi-supervised learning, which uses supplied labels.

findings.original: Official docs label for every source link
findings.reason: Primary evidence now includes a research paper and language draft as well as vendor documentation.

Accepted: authorisation rules can also apply to anonymous requests; OWASP source checked.
Accepted: reachability and application usefulness differ; Python GC/reference evidence checked.
Accepted: direct/mutual self-dependence does not prove termination; source and standard semantic reasoning.
Accepted: unintended event-order dependence need not require simultaneous threads; semantic review, not a new source-specific concurrency experiment.
Accepted: ordinary shared-kernel containers versus Kata VM runtime both checked with their project documentation.
Accepted: TensorFlow SGD update checked; oversized step for x² executed and increases loss1→9.
Accepted: RFC8200 link MTU and path MTU definitions checked; no universal link-frame mapping claim.

checks: Entry ID and alias uniqueness validation
Acronym case sensitivity and Unicode word boundaries
Disconnected anchor and viewport positioning logic
implementation_review.change: Source footer wording now accurate for both documentation and research papers. No functional changes needed.
implementation_review.limit: Static code review and existing Node tests are not a comprehensive browser accessibility, XSS or compatibility audit; parent owns final browser integration.

validation.coverage: All166 entry lookup round-trips; search aliases; Unicode/case/longest matching; protected inline/fenced code and links; HTML escaping; noninteractive mode.

checks: SQLite text PRIMARY KEY accepts NULL in ordinary rowid table
Nullable foreign key accepted with foreign_keys=ON
Oversized gradient step on x² increases loss1→9
Concurrent stale refill after invalidation counterexample

limitations: No low-confidence factual claim remained requiring a visible absence note in this concise glossary scope; this does not certify every possible interpretation or implementation exception.

Confidence labels describe evidence strength, not calibrated correctness probabilities. Medium entries are reliable introductory definitions reviewed semantically but not each freshly retrieved from an external source.
No database, Redis, Kafka or Raft cluster integration experiment was performed for glossary definitions.
Broader diagram/metadata independent review is separately documented in docs/audit-shared-diagrams-metadata.json.
